A series of strongly-fancied European-trained runners failed to deliver at the Breeders’ Cup meeting at Keeneland on Saturday but the visitors finally notched a victory as Benvenuto Cellini and Ryan Moore quickened clear to win the $5m Turf.
Moore was initially expected to ride Diamond Necklace, a stable companion of the winner at the Aidan O’Brien yard, in Saturday’s race, but switched to Benvenuto Cellini after he drew an inside stall.
It proved to be an inspired decision, and Moore found a charmed path to the lead from a position on the inside rail turning in, hitting the front well inside the final furlong on the way to a three-quarter length success.
The win was Aidan O’Brien’s 28 th victory at Group One or Grade One level in 2026, equalling his own record, which was set in 2017. The International meeting in Hong Kong in December will offer him a chance to set a new mark.
“Ryan was calm and relaxed on him and let it happen,” O’Brien said. “He was brilliant on him. He did it again, he had to come out and come round. Time after time he produces on the day. He accepted early he let them go, but he had one bullet to fire which he executed perfectly.”
Benvenuto Cellini is a possible runner in Hong Kong, and will stay in training as a four-year-old next season.
Sovereignty , the 2025 Kentucky Derby winner, was a convincing winner of the most valuable race on the card, the $7m Classic , with Japan’s Forever Young, successful in the race last year, only fifth.
Bill Mott’s four-year-old was a first Classic winner for the Godolphin racing and breeding operation, having also supplied Godolphin’s first win in the Kentucky Derby in 2025.
Earlier on the card, several big names from the European circuit came up short, including Charlie Appleby’s Notable Speech , who finished fast into second place behind Deterministic in his attempt to win the Mile for the second year running.
Blue Bolt , a multiple Group One winner this year, and O’Brien’s filly Precise , the Irish 1,000 Guineas winner, both finished unplaced behind Kathynmarissa in the Filly & Mare Turf, while Wesley Ward’s Bacio, who is trained next to the track, comfortably beat Donnacha O’Brien’s Comanche Brave, the July Cup winner, in the Turf Sprint.
Japan’s big hero came up short but that was a seismic win for the global Godolphin operation, at the end of a day which saw just a single winner from a European stable, but in the most valuable turf race on the card.
It’s been a fascinating couple of days in Kentucky, and the Breeders’ Cup show moves on to Belmont Park next year for the first time since 2005. It will be a very different Belmont Park too, after the New York Racing Association invested around a half-billion dollars in redevelopment.
It sounds very much as though that was Sovereignty’s last trip to the track. He will be off to stud in the morning.
A thoroughly convincing success for Sovereignty , who settled beautifully off the pace set by his stable companion, Knightsbridge, and put the race to bed with a burst of speed at the top of the stretch.
That’s a first ever success in the Classic for the Godolphin operation, delivered by the colt who also supplied their first ever win in the Kentucky Derby win last year.
1. SOVEREIGNTY (Junior Alvarado), 2. The Puma, 3. Knightsbridge. 7 ran.
Down the back, it’s still Knightsbridge in front, Forever Young poised in behind as Sovereignty makes his move …
They’re turning in, it’s going to be a battle for the line … Sovereignty hits the front, he's going a length or two clear, Forever Young looks beaten …
It’s all over and it’s all Sovereignty, last year’s Kentucky Derby winner adds the Classic to his record!
Knightsbridge is straight into the lead, Forever Young is close behind in third …
Golden Tempo is adrift of the field in last, Sovereignty sits fifth…
Off and running in the Breeders’ Cup Classic!
They are going in steadily for the Classic, it won’t be long now …
The pace scenario in the Classic had a shake-up earlier in the week when the much-fancied Magnitude, who likes to set the gallop, was scratched due to injury. His absence could well make life easier for Ryusei Sakai on Forever Young, as he will look to sit in behind a steadier tempo and strike for home at the top of the stretch.
I think, and hope, that Forever Young will stamp his name into Breeders’ Cup history in a few minutes’ time, as he’s a horse that I’ve had a soft spot for ever since his luckless run in the Kentucky Derby. But this is possibly the biggest test of his career, and Sovereignty is currently vying for favouritism with Forever Young at 9-5.
Knightsbridge is a 9-2 shot, while Cherie DeVaux’s Golden Tempo, this year’s Kentucky Derby winner, is popular too with the local punters at 5-1.
22.16 Breeders’ Cup Classic, Grade One, 1m 2f
It feels as though the card has flown by, but now we come to the highlight of the meeting, restored this year to what feels like its rightful position as the final race.
This year’s Classic could also see history made as Japan’s Forever Young attempts to become only the second horse – after Tiznow – ever to go back-to-back in the Breeders’ Cup’s feature event. Yoshito Yahagi’s five-year-old was a half-length winner at Del Mar last November …
… and was also a close third in the 2024 Classic at the same track.
That run came at the end of a three-year-old season when Forever Young also finished third – beaten by a nose and the same – in one of the tightest ever finishes to the Kentucky Derby , having been leant on by Sierra Leone – the 2024 Classic winner – all the way down the stretch. It is a hugely impressive career record overall – he has yet to finish outside the first three in any of his 16 starts – and he is clearly the horse to beat.
There is real depth to the field, though, and Forever Young will finally come face-to-face with Bill Mott’s Sovereignty , the 2025 Kentucky Derby winner, a meeting which was expected to be the highlight of last year’s Breeders’ Cup at Del Mar until Sovereignty was a late scratch due to injury.
He has had a light campaign this season, finishing as the beaten favourite when second in a Grade Two in April and then third in the Grade One Stephen Foster Stakes in June, but he was back in the winner’s enclosure last time when successful in the Grade One Whitney Stakes at Saratoga.
The third horse in this year’s Classic field at single-figure odds is another runner from the Mott stable in Godolphin blue: Knightsbridge, the emphatic winner of the Pacific Classic at Del Mar in August.
The local punters will be pleased with themselves too, they supported Benvenuto Cellini down to start as the 3-1 favourite on the tote.
Ryan Moore opted to jump off Diamond Necklace to ride Benvenuto Cellini from an inside draw and what an inspired choice it proved to be by the best jockey in global racing.
Map Of Stars, who was detached from the field in the early stages, also finished well to take second for James Doyle and Francis-Henri Graffard, suggesting that the pace was off the scale. And Tiffany deserves plaudits too for her fourth-place finish, just behind Diamond Necklace.
1. BENVENUTO CELLINI (Ryan Moore), 2. Map Of Stars, 3. Diamond Necklace. 14 ran.
Ryan Moore has worked wonders to pick a path through the field from the home turn. He was on the rail with a furlong left with a wall of horses in front of him, but when he pulled outside, Benvenuto Cellini took off and ran them down with some ease.
Far Bridge and Minaret Station take the lead, now here’s Deep Monster from Japan going up wide …
Deep Monster leads into the stretch first time, Johanna Walsh and Far Bridge in pursuit ..
Back out past the clubhouse, Bay City Roller only eighth but now making ground …
Benvenuto Cellini on the rail and has only four behind …
Diamond Necklace making ground now, still Deep Monster in front turning for home …
Tiffany and Bay City Roller try to finish, and now here comes Benvenuto Cellini, flying home from off the pace …
He’s going to get there, what a ride by Ryan Moore, Benvenuto Cellini gets the win!
Off and running in the Breeders’ Cup Turf!
A new favourite for the Turf, with the local punters at least: Benvenuto Cellini, the beaten favourite-that-wasn’t in the Derby in June, is now 4-1 on the tote, with Diamond Necklace next in at 9-2.
Burnham Square is the only US-trained runner with any real chance according to the betting, but he was soundly beaten behind Sir Mark Prescott’s admirable globe-trotting mare, Tiffany, and the runner-up, Ethical Diamond, in the Kentucky Turf Cup Invitational at Kentucky Downs last time.
It would be some story if Tiffany could take out today’s race, and add the trophy from the Breeders’ Cup Turf to the one from Alpinista’s win in the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe on the mantlepiece at Sir Mark Prescott’s stable in Newmarket.
After a long series of favourites at or around even-money, we have a favourite at a working-person’s price! Diamond Necklace is a 9-2 shot on the local tote.
9-2 Diamond Necklace 5-1 Benvenuto Cellini & Tiffany 6-1 Bay City Roller 9-1 Burnham Square 12-1 Ethical Diamond 14-1 Survie 20-1 bar
21.36 Breeders’ Cup Turf, Grade One, 1m 4f
It’s been a tricky evening for the Europeans so far but surely, SURELY the visitors will not be leaving this one behind. The top eight in the betting with the British bookies hail from European stables, and there are just three US-trained runners and one from Japan, all outsiders priced up at 22-1 and bigger.
Aidan O’Brien has the top two in the market in Diamond Necklace and Benvenuto Cellini, and they are drawn on opposite sides of the stalls. Diamond Necklace is the marginal favourite, despite a wide draw in 12 that persuaded Ryan Moore to jump ship to Benvenuto Cellini, but she was drawn wide with Soumillon aboard in the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe too and finished a highly creditable third.
Next in the betting is my biggest fancy on tonight’s card, Bay City Roller, who was just in front of Diamond Necklace from a similarly tricky stall at Longchamp and has a string of top-quality performances to his name this season including a Group One win in the Coronation Cup at Epsom in June.
The rain-softened ground may have exaggerated his winning margin but Bay City Roller does not need it soft, as he showed in the Arc. He’s drawn wide, but then he was drawn wide at Longchamp too and had little trouble getting close to the lead. Oisin Murphy is a supreme judge of pace and I can see him producing a bit of a masterclass on Bay City Roller, one of the most consistent and progressive three-year-olds in training.
Another runner to take seriously is last year’s winner, Ethical Diamond, who will set off at a much shorter price this time around. Dylan Browne McMonagle, his imperturbable rider, is perfectly suited to his hold-up style and he will be finishing best of all.
Nitrogen sat just behind the pace in the end, but Jose Ortiz was always going extremely well and once he sent her to the lead, there was going to be only one winner.
She set off as the 3-5 favourite, and we are still waiting for a winner at a double-figure price at this year’s Breeders’ Cup.
1. NITROGEN (Jose Ortiz), 2. Fully Subscribed, 3. Measure. 7 ran.
Off and running in the Breeders’ Cup Distaff!
Super Corredora leads early, Nitrogen back in third.
Fully Subscribed is fifth, the first quarter was modest at 23.57sec.
It’s a steady pace to the half too, Super Corredora has enjoyed a soft lead.
Nitrogen goes outside in the stretch, Fully Subscribed in pursuit, she’s drifting to her right but Nitrogen is clear, she’s at least a length up and here’s the line …
Approaching the stalls for the Distaff, and the punters have swung behind Nitrogen at 3-5, with Fully Subscribed next in.
It will be a considerable shock if the big two are both beaten here, but the three-year-old Super Corredora may have at least a few supporters, having landed a Grade Two at Santa Anita with ease in late September.
20.58 Breeders’ Cup Distaff, Grade One, 1m 1f
But first, we’re back on the dirt for the Distaff, for fillies and mares over a mile and a furlong.
Mark Casse’s four-year-old Nitrogen is likely to set off as the favourite here and boasts a highly impressive career record that includes an emphatic near-13 length success in a Grade One at Saratoga in June.
As the pace map suggests, she is happiest when she makes the running and there is every chance she will get her own way on the lead.
She has a significant market rival, though, in Chad Brown’s Fully Subscribed, who was on the wrong end of that 12 3/4-length beating at Saratoga but has reeled off handsome wins in her last three races including a nine-and-three-quarter length win in the Personal Ensign Stakes at Saratoga in August.
As things stand, Japan could well have more winners on the Breeders’ Cup’s main card than the Europeans, despite fielding far fewer runners. Hopes for a European winner now rest with a strong contingent of runners in the Turf in two races’ time.
A valiant effort by Notable Speech to run down the winner but the favourite came up short. William Buick had four behind him and was three wide around the final turn, and had five lengths to make on Deterministic at the top of the stretch, which proved to be too big an ask.
Deterministic was sent off at 5-1, while Notable Speech was the evens favourite on the tote.
1. DETERMINISTIC (Kendrick Carmouche), 2. Notable Speech, 3. Lake Forest. 13 ran.
Puerto Rico slow away but makes rapid ground to sit second, True Love towards the rear …
Now Cabo Spirit settles on the lead, Deterministic next and Puerto Rico third …
Into the far turn, Notable Speech is a long way off the lead, …
Deterministic leads into the final furlong, Notable Speech is finishing fast from way off the pace, making ground with every stride …
Will he get there? No, he had too much ground to make up and it’s Deterministic for the win
They’re going into the gates for the Mile … And they’re off and running!
I’m sticking with Notable Speech here but 4-5 is very short. And the Brighton fan in me would love to see the blue-and-white stripes first across the line aboard Lake Forest.
4-5 Notable Speech 9-2 Deterministic 8-1 Rhetorical 9-1 Lake Forest 12-1 Ask Ikigomi 15-1 True Love 18-1 bar
Aidan O’Brien, True Love’s trainer, also has Puerto Rico in this race, although he’s drawn wide in stall 14. And there’s a couple of Japanese-trained runners too, in Ask Ikigomi and Lugal, and the former has at least an each-way chance on ratings having been edged out by a nose in a Grade One at Tokyo last time.
After the Euro-wobble in the first two races on the card, there could be no better trainer than Charlie Appleby to get the bandwagon rolling again, in a contest where he has a near-perfect record of four wins from five starters.
Notable Speech, last year’s winner, won with something to spare and has looked every bit as good, if not better, so far this year, including when successful in the Grade One Woodbine Mile last time with his leading US-trained rival, Deterministic, in second.
Notable Speech will set off as a short-priced and worthy favourite but faces some stern opposition, including Lake Forest, who runs in the blue-and-white colours of Tony Bloom and will bid to set the seal on a perfect day for the owner of Brighton & Hove Albion after their magnificent victory at Manchester City earlier on.
Lake Forest did not have any luck in running when second over today’s course-and-distance in the Turf Mile last time out.
And there is a Classic winner in the field too, as True Love took the 1,000 Guineas at Newmarket back in May.
There’s no way Englishman was beaten by his draw there, he was just beaten by a better horse on the day. T O Elvis was at least eight lengths adrift when Englishman hit the lead two out, but he showed incredible finishing speed to stay on all the way up the stretch and grab the lead two strides from the line
Liam Smith, meanwhile, did not drop away after being passed and rewarded his each-way backers by staying on well for third.
1. T O ELVIS (Ryusei Sakai), 2. Englishman, 3. Liam Smith. 13 ran.
Englishman fast away but he’s three wide …
Now Englishman settles second after a quarter, Liam Smith is leading.
Englishman takes Liam Smith and goes into the lead, he leads by two halfway down the stretch
But here’s T O Elvis for Japan, he trying to chase down the favourite, gaining all the time and YES! he’s got there, T O Elvis is a big winner on the dirt for Japan.
Off and running in the Breeders’ Cup Sprint!
The local punters are unconcerned by Englishman’s wide draw and he’s 4-5 on the tote.
4-5 Englishman 5-2 T O Elvis 6-1 Listenupshance 14-1 Built 19-1 Liam Smith 25-1 bar
Englishman is a clear form pick but he’s drawn in stall 13 and unlikely to get across to the lead with the speedy Mad House drawn one. T O Elvis, meanwhile, is only two stalls closer to the rail in 11, though he a more of a closer.
It’s a definite stab in the dark, but Liam Smith has posted some useful numbers while moving through the ranks and is well drawn to attack in stall three. At around 25-1 with the British bookies, I’m going to take a small each-way interest.
19.42 Breeders’ Cup Sprint, Grade One, 6f
But before we get to the Mile, there’s another hot favourite looming on the horizon in the shape of Englishman, in the Sprint on the dirt.
Cherie DeVaux’s three-year-old has won three of his four starts this season including a dominant success in the H Allen Jerkens Memorial over seven furlongs at Saratoga last time.
The second-pick in the betting is the Japanese-trained T O Elvis, the winner of his last five starts but not seen out since an impressive success at Churchill Downs in May.
And there’s also an interesting outsider on an upward curve in Peter Miller’s Liam Smith, who has emerged via claimers but posted a very impressive time when successful at Santa Anita last time.
Saturday is not unfolding as European racing fans might have hoped so far, but Notable Speech is up next in the Mile in two races’ time while the Turf will surely go to a visitor – it’s just a question of which one.
Looping back to the Turf Sprint earlier on the card, Bacio is syndicate-owned and Wesley Ward was particularly pleased about that as his daughter-in-law, Caitlin, helped to keep Bacio in his yard when offers came in for him earlier in his career.
double quotation mark There was a lot to the whole story behind him, to me getting him, and then once he started winning, me keeping him. He was a sought after horse, a lot of people were coming in. My daughter-in-law brought me one of the greatest gifts ever, my grandson, Killian, and she put an ownership group together with MyRacehorse in order to keep him here in our stable.
It’s so nice to have thousands of owners in this horse and win the Breeders’ Cup, it’s going to really help our sport.
A big let down for the Europeans, neither Blue Bolt nor Precise was ever travelling with purpose and both were beaten before the final turn. Well done to County Kildare-based Willie McCreery though – his 25-1 outsider Jancis came through to finish third, and best of the Euro runners.
Kathynmarissa was sent off at 5-1 on the local tote, but there was 7-1 and 8-1 on offer with British firms beforehand.
1. KATHYNMARISSA (Jose Ortiz), 2. Gimme A Nother, 3. Jancis. 12 ran.
Kathynmarissa lands the spoils, Precise and Blue Bolt both soundly beaten.
Into the turn, it’s still Classic Q, Precise looks beaten, now Gimme A Nother goes on with a furlong to run …
But here’s Kathynmarissa, she’s making rapid ground and she’s going to get there …
Down the back, Classic Q still leads, Precise under a slight drive, Blue Bolt makes a move three wide …
Classic Q turns first, Precise three wide in mid-division and Blue Bolt has three behind her

## कीनलैंड में ब्रीडर्स कप का रोमांचक समापन

कीनलैंड में आयोजित ब्रीडर्स कप प्रतियोगिता के दूसरे दिन यूरोपीय धावकों को शुरुआती झटकों का सामना करना पड़ा, लेकिन अंततः बेनवेनुतो सेलिनी ने रयान मूर के साथ शानदार प्रदर्शन करते हुए $50 लाख की टर्फ रेस अपने नाम कर ली। 

## मुख्य परिणाम और जीत

* **टर्फ रेस:** बेनवेनुतो सेलिनी ने शानदार वापसी करते हुए तीन-चौथाई लंबाई से जीत दर्ज की। यह एडन ओ'ब्रायन के लिए 2026 में 28वीं ग्रुप वन या ग्रेड वन जीत रही।
* **क्लासिक रेस:** 2025 के केंटकी डर्बी विजेता सॉवरएल्टी ने $70 लाख की क्लासिक रेस में शानदार जीत हासिल की। यह गॉल्फिन रेसिंग और ब्रीडिंग ऑपरेशन के लिए पहली क्लासिक जीत है।
* **अन्य परिणाम:** डर्ट माइल, स्प्रिंट और डिस्टैफ श्रेणियों में भी कड़ा मुकाबला देखने को मिला, जहाँ नाइट्रोजन ने जोस ऑर्टिज़ के मार्गदर्शन में डिस्टैफ रेस में जीत हासिल की।

## आगे की प्रक्रिया और सत्यापन

प्रशंसक और विश्लेषक आधिकारिक परिणाम और भविष्य के आयोजनों की जानकारी के लिए न्यू यॉर्क रेसिंग एसोसिएशन या आधिकारिक ब्रीडर्स कप घोषणाओं की जाँच कर सकते हैं। प्रतियोगिता का अगला चरण आने वाले समय में बेलमॉन्ट पार्क में आयोजित होने की उम्मीद है।

en_body:
European-trained runners faced a challenging outing at the Breeders' Cup meeting at Keeneland, securing just a single victory on the card, though it came in the high-profile $5m Turf courtesy of Benvenuto Cellini and jockey Ryan Moore. 

Moore executed a late surge from the inside rail to secure a three-quarter length victory. The triumph marked Aidan O'Brien's 28th victory at Group One or Grade One level in 2026, tying the record he established in 2017. O'Brien noted that Moore maintained composure throughout the race, expertly navigating traffic to secure the win.

## Feature Race Results

* **Breeders' Cup Classic ($7m):** Won by Sovereignty, the 2025 Kentucky Derby winner trained by Bill Mott. The victory marked a first Classic success for the Godolphin racing and breeding operation. Last year's winner, Japan's Forever Young, finished fifth.
* **Breeders' Cup Turf ($5m):** Won by Benvenuto Cellini, ridden by Ryan Moore.
* **Breeders' Cup Mile:** Won by Deterministic, defeating the previous year's winner, Notable Speech.
* **Breeders' Cup Sprint:** Won by T O Elvis, representing Japan.
* **Breeders' Cup Distaff:** Won by Nitrogen under jockey Jose Ortiz.

## International Contenders and Future Venues

Several prominent European contenders fell short during the Saturday card. Charlie Appleby's Notable Speech finished second behind Deterministic in the Mile, while multiple Group One winner Blue Bolt and the Irish 1,000 Guineas winner Precise finished unplaced in the Filly & Mare Turf.

The Breeders' Cup is scheduled to move to Belmont Park next year for the first time since 2005, following significant redevelopments by the New York Racing Association.

## Verification and Practical Information

Official results, race replays, and full event statistics can be verified through the official Breeders' Cup website or recognized racing authorities such as Equibase.
